sec: Hypertension 2023 · endocrine secondary causes, work-up and treatment indications

items.q: Match each monogenic form with the renin and aldosterone pattern printed for it — 1) Liddle syndrome 2) Apparent mineralocorticosteroid excess 3) Glucocorticoid remediable hyperaldosteronism … A) Low renin with low aldosterone B) Low renin with high aldosterone
items.exp: ENaC activation in Liddle syndrome and the cortisol excess of apparent mineralocorticoid excess both suppress renin and aldosterone, whereas the ACTH-driven chimeric gene of glucocorticoid remediable aldosteronism gives low renin with high aldosterone. (Book p979)

items.q: Which mechanism is written beside Geller's syndrome in the genetic list?
opts: Gain of function of the mineralocorticosteroid receptor
Loss of function of 11-beta hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase
Activation of the epithelial sodium channel
Chimeric gene formation under ACTH control
items.exp: Geller's syndrome is the entry annotated as a mineralocorticosteroid receptor gain of function, distinct from the ENaC activation of Liddle syndrome and the ACTH-driven chimera of GRA. (Book p979)

items.q: Assess the bracket drawn beside the genetic list: I It reads hypertension with metabolic alkalosis and hypokalemia. II Gordon's syndrome shares that biochemical pattern.
items.exp: The bracket gives hypertension, metabolic alkalosis and hypokalemia for the Liddle and apparent mineralocorticoid excess group, while Gordon's syndrome is written on the opposite side of the comparison with hyperkalemia and acidosis. (Book p979)

items.q: Phaetype IV or Gordon's syndrome is described with all of the following EXCEPT:
items.exp: The Gordon's column lists hyperkalemia, acidosis, hypertension and the reverse Gitelman's annotation, and potassium is high rather than low. (Book p979)

items.q: Compare the two pseudohypoaldosteronism columns: I PHA type I is entered with hyperkalemia, acidosis and a normal to low blood pressure. II The distinguishing feature drawn between type I and Gordon's syndrome is the blood pressure.
items.exp: Both columns share hyperkalemia and acidosis, and what separates them on the page is the pressure, with hypertension in Gordon's syndrome and normal to low pressure in type I. (Book p979)

items.q: The triad of primary hyperaldosteronism printed under the acquired column consists of which three findings?
items.exp: The acquired list opens with the primary hyperaldosteronism triad of HTN, m alkalosis and hypokalemia, then continues with Cushing syndrome, phaeochromocytoma, acromegaly, raised thyroid hormones, hypothyroidism and raised PTH. (Book p979)

items.q: All of these appear in the acquired endocrine list EXCEPT:
items.exp: The acquired column names primary hyperaldosteronism, Cushing syndrome, phaeochromocytoma, acromegaly, raised T3 and T4, hypothyroidism and a raised PTH; Addison's disease is not part of it. (Book p979)

items.q: Which study is labelled the first investigation when secondary hypertension is being worked up?
items.exp: The investigation branch for secondary HTN marks USG with renal artery doppler as the 1st investigation, before the renal function, urine albumin to creatinine and hormonal panels. (Book p979)

items.q: Match each investigation with the purpose it serves on this page — 1) 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines 2) TFT and PTH 3) Urine albumin to creatinine ratio … A) Thyroid and parathyroid causes B) A phaeochromocytoma screen C) A marker of hypertensive renal damage alongside RFT
items.exp: The investigations are grouped as the doppler study, the renal damage markers of urine albumin to creatinine and RFT, the electrolyte and hormonal panel of sodium, potassium, calcium, phosphate, metanephrines, TFT and PTH, plus LVH and retinopathy as target-organ findings. (Book p979)

items.q: Which measurement is called the best indicator of target organ damage?
items.exp: The last entry of the investigation row is central systolic blood pressure, annotated as the best indicator of target organ damage. (Book p979)

items.q: Below what age, and with how many drugs in a regimen, does this page prompt a search for secondary hypertension?
opts: Below 40 years, and uncontrolled on 3 drugs including a diuretic
Below 50 years, and uncontrolled on 2 drugs
Below 30 years, and uncontrolled on 4 drugs excluding a diuretic
Any age, provided 3 drugs are prescribed without a diuretic
items.exp: The three prompting factors are hypertension below 40 years, resistant hypertension defined as uncontrolled on 3 drugs including diuretics, and hypertension with target organ damage. (Book p979)

items.q: Match each treatment threshold with the printed instruction — 1) 130/80 mmHg with coronary artery disease 2) 140/90 mmHg, grade 1, with no organ damage 3) 150/95 mmHg … A) Start medication at once B) Start monotherapy C) Four weeks of lifestyle changes first
items.exp: Coronary disease takes monotherapy from 130/80, grade 1 without mediated damage gets four weeks of lifestyle measures, and 150/95 goes straight to medication. (Book p979)

items.q: Fill up: The four-week lifestyle block asks for weight reduction, a diet with ______ salt and ______ potassium and magnesium, more physical activity, reduced smoking and ______.
items.exp: The five lifestyle lines are weight reduction, a diet with a fall in salt and rises in potassium and magnesium, increased physical activity, reduced smoking and reduced stress. (Book p979)

items.q: Assess the escalation rule and the targets: I If blood pressure does not change after four weeks of lifestyle measures, a minimum of two drugs is started. II The target is 120 to 130 over 70 to 80 in patients below 65 years and 130 to 140 over 80 to 90 in those above 65.
items.exp: The arrow labelled no change in BP leads to start with minimum 2 drugs, and the two target lines are printed by age band exactly as stated. (Book p979)

items.q: A 58-year-old with newly detected hypertension at 146/92 mmHg has no organ damage, no diabetes and no cardiovascular disease. What does this page's algorithm do first?
opts: Four weeks of lifestyle measures, then two drugs if the BP does not change
items.exp: A reading of 146/92 falls in the 140/90 grade 1 box without mediated organ damage, which the flowchart sends to four weeks of lifestyle change before starting a minimum of two drugs. (Book p979)

items.q: Which of the following would NOT by itself prompt a search for secondary hypertension according to the list on this page?
opts: Onset at 55 years with BP controlled on amlodipine
Resistant hypertension on three drugs including a diuretic
items.exp: The three prompting factors are age under 40, resistance on three drugs including a diuretic and target organ damage; a well-controlled 55-year-old meets none of them. (Book p979)
